quote: Life is not a series of gig lamps symmetrically arranged; life is a luminous halo, a semi-transparent envelope surrounding us from the beginning of consciousness to the end.
source: Virginia Woolf, Modern Fiction, The Common Reader (Hogarth Press, 1925)
note: Corrected the wording. The Common Reader of 1925 reads life is a luminous halo. The reading but a luminous halo belongs to the earlier version of the essay, Modern Novels, printed in the Times Literary Supplement in 1919.

evidence.where: Full text of The Common Reader, First Series at Project Gutenberg Australia, downloaded and read directly at the Modern Fiction essay; the sentence follows the passage on an ordinary mind on an ordinary day and precedes Is it not the task of the novelist.
evidence.edition: The Common Reader, First Series (1925), Modern Fiction
evidence.locator: Modern Fiction, the paragraph beginning Examine for a moment an ordinary mind on an ordinary day

reason: The passage is in Modern Fiction where claimed, but the proposal carried the 1919 Modern Novels reading, which breaks the semicolon into a fragment. The Common Reader text repeats the word life and that is the wording now supplied.
